subject: Netpath preflight: streaming QoS, VPN/peering, and PoC window
messages:
From: Aisha Gupta <aisha@finexa.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Finexa Networking Team <netops@finexa.com>
Date: 2027-08-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up from today's discovery — latency & streaming targets

Thanks for the call this morning — useful overview. A quick recap of the items Finexa needs help validating before we agree to a PoC: 

- Latency targets: 95th percentile for tail latency (single-turn text generation) should be <= 120ms from our app tier (ap-south-west host) to response-ready token on a 2k seq.
- Streaming: we plan to open up to 40 concurrent streaming connections (user-facing live transcripts). Per-stream steady-state throughput ~250 tokens/minute, bursts up to 800 tokens/minute for ~30s.
- Concurrency & throughput: sustained QPS estimate 180 requests/min (avg 700 tokens/request), peak bursts to 700 QPS for short windows.
- Network topology: we will route via a VPN to a Redwood-dedicated peering peer (details in attached diagram). Egress path includes our NAT gateway, then a cloud egress IP.
- Security: TLS termination will be on our edge (we expect mutual TLS for the tunnel).

Questions we had that would affect acceptance criteria: 
1) How does Redwood measure streaming tail latency (per-chunk vs total first-byte)?
2) Any recommendations on internal buffering to keep latency below 120ms 95p?
3) Will Redwood need inbound ports opened or is everything initiated from our side over the VPN?

Attached: initial network topology PNG.

Can you confirm if the above is doable and outline next steps for a brief perf preflight and a proposed PoC window (we'd like to run tests week of Aug 16).

Thanks,
Aisha
Network & Infrastructure Lead
Finexa

[Attachment: network_topology.png (PNG, 318 KB)]

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Gupta <aisha@finexa.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery — latency & streaming targets

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear recap, very helpful. Short answers up front: yes, we can validate the targets; some of the acceptance criteria will be shaped by where TLS terminates and whether you can route traffic through a single egress IP during the PoC. 

Proposed next steps: 
- Jordan (cc'd) will share a concise preflight checklist + required test harness endpoints. Can you confirm whether the PoC traffic will originate from your staging VPC or from a set of user devices (edge)?
- We'll schedule a 60 minute perf-preflight on Aug 10 to align on measurement methods (first-byte vs per-chunk latency) and to confirm the VPN peering config. Suggest Aug 10 10:00 PT — does that work?
- If the preflight looks good we'll run a 3-day PoC starting Aug 16 that includes: 1) streaming throughput run, 2) tail-latency smoke tests at 2k seq, 3) concurrency ramp to peak bursts.

Notes: we measure streaming latency both as first-byte and 95p per-chunk; for your target we recommend looking at first-byte 95p < 80ms for doorbell responsiveness and per-chunk 95p < 120ms for overall UX. We'll provide scripts that simulate your burst patterns.

I'll also add a short checklist (from Jordan) with the networking items we need to confirm.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Aisha Gupta <aisha@finexa.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-03T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery — latency & streaming targets

Thanks — attaching a short preflight checklist (XLSX) and a script list for the perf harness. High level items we need from Finexa to avoid surprises during the PoC: 

- Egress IPs: provide the IPs that the VPN will NAT to so we can whitelist / route back appropriately. If you have multiple egress IPs please indicate sticky session behavior.
- TLS termination: confirm whether mTLS will terminate at your edge or at a load balancer inside the private network. If we terminate at the Redwood side we need to exchange certs and confirm cipher suites.
- MTU & jumbo frames: confirm MTU on the site-to-site link (we prefer 1500 unless you can support 9000 for higher throughput runs).
- Packet inspection / proxy: confirm no inline proxy or DPI will be modifying TCP windows or TLS.
- Sequence length and tokenization: confirm expected average and 95p token lengths (you called out 700 tokens/request avg — please confirm distribution if you have it).
- Test accounts: create 3 staging accounts (low, med, high concurrency) with tokens we can use for the PoC.

Measurement approach: we will run two harnesses simultaneously — (a) streaming harness (per-chunk latency, per-stream token rate) and (b) batch harness (single-turn generation for tail-latency). We'll provide Grafana dashboards and a quick Slack alert hook to your netops channel for real-time failures.

Proposed PoC timeline: 
- Aug 10: preflight call + checklist review
- Aug 12-13: configuration window (VPN + firewall rules)
- Aug 16-18: PoC runs (3-day window)

Attachments: redwood_perf_checklist.xlsx (contains required ports, sample iptables rules and a minimal k6 + python harness).

Jordan Blake
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
[jordan_blake@redwood.com]

[Attachment: redwood_perf_checklist.xlsx (XLSX, 56 KB)]

From: Aisha Gupta <aisha@finexa.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Finexa Networking Team <netops@finexa.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-04T15:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery — latency & streaming targets

Great — thanks Jordan and Camila. Confirming the following from our side: 

- Egress IPs: 54.191.23.44, 54.191.23.45 (we will NAT outbound PoC traffic to .44 for consistency)
- TLS: mTLS terminates at our edge LB (we control certs), tunnel will be site-to-site IPSec with mutual auth.
- MTU: standard 1500 on the VPN.
- No DPI / proxy in the path.
- Token lengths: attached a small histogram (in the Drive link) but 700 tokens/request avg looks correct; 95p ~ 1,200 tokens.
- Test accounts: we will provision the three staging tokens and share them in the secure Drive folder by Aug 9.

Agree to the Aug 10 preflight at 10:00 PT and the PoC window Aug 16-18. Sharing the Drive folder and DocuSign link for the MSA now.

Thanks — Aisha
Aisha Gupta
Network & Infrastructure Lead, Finexa
